newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin to have heart bypass operation - Interfax.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin to have heart bypass operation - Interfax.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin will have a heart bypass operation for ischaemic disease at Moscow's Cardiological Centre, a senior Russian surgeon told Interfax news agency on Friday.

Professor Valery Sadrikov, deputy director of the Surgical Centre of the Academy of Sciences, did not say when the operation would take place. Yeltsin said on Thursday he would have a heart operation at the end of September but gave no details.

Yeltsin did not make clear what he was suffering from, referring generally to "heart disease" and it was not clear until Friday whether the operation would be a fairly routine bypass procedure or a more serious treatment.

"The operation on the Russian president's heart will be carried out at the Cardiological Centre of Academician Chazov," Sadrikov told Interfax. Leading heart specialist Yevgeny Chazov himself declined to confirm in an earlier interview with Interfax that his centre would conduct the operation.
Yeltsin was twice hospitalised last year with ischaemic heart disease -- a reduction in the blood supply to the heart usually caused by a clogging of the cardiac arteries.

Sadrikov said the president would undergo "a shunt of the vessels which supply blood to the heart". The operation means a bypass in which a vein or an artery from the patient's leg or elsewhere is grafted in to divert blood around the blockage.
